card.name: Yankadi & Macru
card.tagline: Susu paired courtship/seduction dance of coastal Guinea
card.profile: Yankadi and Macru (Makru/Makuru) are paired Susu (Soso) dances from southwestern coastal Guinea (and northwestern Sierra Leone), collectively the 'rhythm of courtship' (Leicestershire Music; mandebala.net). The dance begins slowly with Yankadi - girls and boys face each other in two rows and dance slowly toward one another; a boy places a scarf on a girl as a symbol of love. A whistle then signals the change to the faster Macru, the rows break up and couples dance individually (Mamady Keita, A Life for the Djembe, via Leicestershire Music). 'Yankadi' is glossed as 'it is good (to be here)'.
card.insight: Master djembefola Famoudou Konate has quipped that 'many marriages have taken place as a result of Yankadi Makru celebrations'; the pairing is danced by Susu, Mande and Temne across Forecariah, Dubreka, Coyah, Kindia, Boffa and Boke (Djembefola forum, citing Moustapha Bangoura).
card.image_significance: A two-speed dance of seduction. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — coastal (Susu), Guinea.
